title: Comparing leaders: Kelly Martin's tight ship and Earl Hines's showmanship
summary: Kelly Martin was firm and strict about punctuality and professionalism, while Hines was a flamboyant showman who taught him about the stage.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Before we get too much further, I want to compare a few of these people, just as you dealt with them as leaders, these different leaders: Kelly Martin and Earl Hines and Tiny Bradshaw.
Maybe go back and, say the transition from Kelly Martin to Earl Hines...You marked Kelly Martin as the first person you went into the big time with.

Yes. Well, Kelly Martin was a good band leader and he loved music, but he was a firm band leader. He kept everybody in line. Of course he didn't have any trouble out of me because it was all so exciting to me, you know what I mean, but he ran a nice tight ship. And then when I got with Earl Hines it was a different thing all together, you know, he was so flamboyant and so much charisma. I mean I don't think he even noticed I was there, really, you know what I mean, because he was a showman, see. But he didn't bother anyone either. That's when I really saw what it's
like being on the stage, you know, out into the lime-light, you know what I mean. And that was a revelation to me. It all didn't come to me at once, but, you know, I look back and it impressed me.
When you mentioned that Kelly Martin ran a tight ship, were there rules that you all had to observe?

Oh yeah. You had to be on time and you be neat and clean and play, you know, Play the right notes, you know what I mean, and be a professional. No foolin' around, you know what I mean. And that's the way it was. And that's the way he was able to keep that job, because Slim Jones, he had confidence in him and, you know, it was a steady job, it was the best job in Detroit.
